utterances.text: You mentioned that this commission, this commission worked in the KP Dom and made inventories of the various sections, especially the warehouses. The warehouses in the KP Dom, how many warehouses were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: There was a central warehouse with materials for the furniture factory and the other plants, all except the catering unit. That was a central warehouse for the furniture, the metalworking unit. Then there was another warehouse for the farm outside the compound and then there was one for the canteen and one for food for the inmates. I know that those warehouses existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the Exhibit 6, the big -- the bigger plan. Yes, both.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You do not need to point out the storage places of the factories. Just show me the storage place, the food storage place. Where was this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: I find it hard to orient myself. This sketch is not clear to me. Can I turn it like this? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Have a look first to orient yourself and then we put it back.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Just so -- let me see. Let me see. You asked about which warehouse? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the food. Where the food for the KP Dom was stored.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Here, building number 1, and it was in the basement. No, sorry, on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Does that mean it was below Room 11? Is that the storage place, below Room 11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps a photograph might be better.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just looking for the photographs. Yes. It's the photo 7476. Yes. You can replace it, yes. The top photo, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that the food -- where the food was stored?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Evidently, because that's what the sign says, and the sign was made by me in the printing press. It says here, "Warehouse for Convicts' Food."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's what we've been calling the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. That's all right. We've got our terminology straight now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You can put this away.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It says the food for the convicts. Was there another food -- another storage place for food in the KP Dom, and if so, where was that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Unprocessed food, that is, eggs, were kept at the farm and were used to supply the town. Before the war, in the canteen and in the Brioni Motel, there was a small storage area for raw materials such as meat, milk, and other foodstuffs, but during the war, I don't know what happened to that. This commission made an inventory, but I really have no idea how much food was left.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show you the photo 7512.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You see the ground floor -- the basement or ground floor. Was food stored in building 2, ground floor, as well or, rather, basement, below the ground floor? You see this little door, this little door and the few windows. What was stored -- yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: You mean this here?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. What was stored there? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Before I retired, I know that there were big barrels for making sauerkraut here for the convicts. You know, this was the sort of food that we used in the winter. And later on, I don't know what was kept there. It was probably used for the same purpose, but we didn't have cabbage.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And during the war, was there also other food stored in there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned that food was transported to the central kitchen. What do you mean by "central kitchen"?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Well, that was the only kitchen that existed. Before the war we called it the central kitchen because there was a kitchen in the restaurant or, rather, the canteen as well and then there was another one at the Brioni Motel. So it was probably a slip when I said "central kitchen," because it was the only kitchen during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Maybe I misunderstood you when you gave your testimony. I understood that food from the KP Dom was transported somewhere else and then returned in portions whenever it was needed. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: I didn't say that. Food was prepared in that kitchen and distributed in that kitchen. I don't remember having said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Maybe because you used the words "central kitchen" that I thought it was something else, but when you said "central kitchen," it was the kitchen in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Yes. It was the only kitchen. And we all took our food there, all the inmates, the employees, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the food storage of the Brioni Hotel was at the Brioni Hotel or where?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: That was a motel, not a hotel - just a small correction - and the storage was for making meat dishes to serve to the guests. Before the war, the motel worked well. It was -- so it was just an auxiliary sort of storage area where food was kept that was prepared for the guests before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you said that inventories of all these warehouses were made, and you also mentioned a warehouse for inmates of the KP Dom. Do you mean this storage place that you pointed out on the photo, or was there another warehouse for inmates?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: No. No. There was one storage area, only one, for all, and food was kept there. The conditions were good, because it was in the basement, it was big, the temperature was right. So everything was kept there, for the inmates, for the employees, for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the hygienic necessities, where were these things stored? Hygienic necessities, blankets, such things, where were they?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you said that inventories were made, and what about the food situation? For how many weeks was food stored there? Can you say anything about the capacity that you found there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: I didn't say I was in the commission that took inventories in other parts of the unit. They visited all the units, including the printing press. I was not a member of that commission, so I don't know what amounts of food there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. While you worked as a guard, you got your tasks from Mr. Rasevic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: From Mr. Rasevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You did not get orders from Mr. Todovic; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Todovic was in charge of the military part of the KP Dom. It was only later.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I just asked -- I don't want you to repeat this so often. We have heard it enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, there's one thing that it does give rise to. I think you should ask him specifically: Does he say that Mr. Todovic had nothing to do with the Muslim detainees?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, I'm coming to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, you're coming to it. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I was only asking him: You personally did not get any orders from Mr. Todovic while you were on guard duty; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: Mr. Todovic was in charge of questioning detainees, and my superior for guard duty was exclusively Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will talk about Mr. Todovic and his position tomorrow at length. When you -- just one more question related to Mr. Rasevic. When something happened that was important, you reported this to Mr. Rasevic; right? If you had anything unusual, you reported to Mr. Rasevic, right, in relation to guard duty?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: My superior at guard duty was the person who was on duty at the Dom, and then the hierarchy went on. So while I was doing guard duty, my superior was the one who was on duty for the Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you inform him verbally or did you put something down in writing?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR DOLAS
utterances.text: No. Nothing was done in writing. It was just oral. The guard duty would be handed over, another two guards would arrive, we would report to the one on duty and he would tell us we were free to go until it was my turn again, and that wasn't very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, it's 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Again, it's after 4.00, but nevertheless we will adjourn now. We'll resume at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of May, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.02 p.m.,
